name: Northstar AI
description: Fictional B2B AI SaaS company selling Beacon, a permission-aware workplace knowledge search product. This is an authored simulation, not a real Slack export. Every person, customer, ticket, metric, and policy is invented for this assignment.

channels.name: eng-platform
channels.purpose: Implementation, reliability, integrations, and permission enforcement

channels.name: sales-deals
channels.purpose: Qualification, pilots, pricing, forecasts, and sales handoffs

channels.name: support-triage
channels.purpose: Customer tickets, workarounds, escalations, and incident resolution

channels.name: csm-accounts
channels.purpose: Onboarding, adoption, success plans, and renewal health

channels.name: ops-business
channels.purpose: Finance, security reviews, people operations, and internal coordination

messages.text: Harbor Health has 18k files waiting in the Drive connector. Google is returning 429s and every worker retries after exactly 30 seconds. We are creating our own traffic spike. Tracking ENG-241.
Add exponential backoff with jitter and cap concurrency at four workers per tenant. Do not raise the shared quota; Cedar is syncing normally on the same project.
Patch is in staging. A throttled tenant now backs off independently and the oldest-file-age metric starts falling. I will canary Harbor tomorrow at 14:00 UTC.

threads.title: SUP-108: newly uploaded policies not showing

messages.text: Harbor Health uploaded revised leave policies this morning. Direct Drive links work, but Beacon still returns last week's version. First report came in at 15:55 UTC.
Permissions look correct. Connector status says connected, but the oldest pending file is 96 minutes old. I am escalating freshness rather than asking the customer to reconnect.
Engineering is tracking this as ENG-241: synchronized retries after Google rate limits. Patch canary is tomorrow. Existing indexed documents remain searchable.
Summit Legal is interested in Beacon for 240 staff, but procurement will not move until they review the SOC 2 report and our data-processing agreement. Target signature is September 30.
Their technical lead also asked whether document content is used to train shared models. Our current policy is no training on customer content.
I can send the restricted assurance packet once their NDA is signed. Use the approved questionnaire responses; do not attach internal incident notes to the sales deck.
Harbor's new-hire cohort starts September 21. Their champion needs the revised leave and equipment policies in search before training. Today's freshness issue is blocking my checklist.
We can still prepare the workshop using the synthetic practice workspace. I will not ask attendees to validate against stale customer policies.
SUP-108 is linked to ENG-241. I will send you a verified recovery update after the queue clears; connector connected status alone is not enough.
Please submit September vendor invoices by 17:00 UTC on September 28. Include the purchase owner, approved amount, and service period. A Slack thumbs-up is not a purchase order.
If the supplier changed bank details, route it through the callback verification process before payment. Do not verify the change using the phone number in the change-request email.
I will remind the team leads. Personal expense reimbursements use the expense form and should not go into the vendor invoice queue.
ENG-241 is live for Harbor Health only. Queue is draining at roughly 900 files/minute and 429s have dropped. Keeping the rollout paused until we see a full hour without retries bunching up.
Ticket SUP-108 confirms new documents are appearing again. Their admin asked whether they need to disconnect Google Drive. I told them to leave the connection in place.
15:10 UTC update: backlog cleared, freshness back below five minutes. Released the worker change globally. No reconnect or document reupload needed.
Harbor's admin confirmed all three revised leave policies now appear. Queue cleared at 15:10 UTC after the connector retry fix. Closing the active incident portion of SUP-108.
Please say ingestion was delayed; we have no evidence that files were deleted. Send the incident timeline and the next freshness check time, not internal speculation.
I will check with their champion on Thursday. They have onboarding next week, so confidence in document freshness matters as much as today's fix.
Cedar's pilot should answer questions across engineering runbooks and onboarding docs. They keep asking how many tokens we support, but the business problem is time spent hunting for an owner.
Let's agree on twenty real employee questions and measure whether the correct source is in the first five results. They want at least sixteen successes before buying.
I will recruit one champion from IT and one from engineering. We can measure search adoption separately; a one-time guided demo is not evidence of sustained use.
Summit's NDA is signed. The approved assurance packet includes the current SOC 2 Type II report, subprocessor list, and data-processing agreement. Access is restricted to their named reviewers.
Thanks. Their questionnaire asks if customer content trains a shared model. I have “no” from the approved response library; checking before I submit.
That remains the approved answer. Also state the actual hosting and telemetry regions; the report does not imply every service runs in the customer's chosen region.

threads.title: SAML login loop at Cedar Labs

messages.text: Cedar staff authenticate with Okta and land back on our login page. Only their production SAML app fails; the test app works. Ticket SUP-112.
The production app has the old ACS callback URL. Compare it with the exact value shown in Beacon admin, including the tenant slug. Clearing browser cookies will not fix that mismatch.
Admin corrected the callback and two affected users signed in. Asked them to keep one break-glass admin account outside SAML during future identity changes.

threads.title: Removed Slack members can still see cached citations

messages.text: Found a stale permission cache when a user leaves a private Slack channel. Search could keep returning the old citation until the cache expired. Reproduced with test accounts; tracking SEC-18.
Treat membership removal as an invalidation event. Until that lands, disable the result cache for private channels. We should fail closed if the membership lookup times out.
Fix deployed at 18:00 UTC. Membership is rechecked at retrieval time and removed users get no results from that channel. Added a revoke-access regression case; public-channel search is unaffected.

threads.title: Morrow asks for an end-of-quarter discount

messages.text: Morrow Logistics asked for 18% off the annual Growth renewal if they sign this week. They are comparing our annual price with a competitor's monthly price, which is confusing the conversation.
Up to 10% is within the approved annual-prepay policy. Anything larger needs Dana's written approval and a clear commercial reason. Avoid stacking an extra discount on pilot credits.
I sent an apples-to-apples annual comparison with a 10% concession. Leaving the opportunity in negotiation until procurement confirms the term.
Ran the twenty-question Cedar baseline. Employees found the correct source within five results on fourteen questions. Most misses involve acronyms that never appear in the document titles.
The agreed purchase gate is sixteen of twenty. Let's preserve the same questions for the final check rather than replace the hard ones.
Also recording median lookup time: 4m 20s today. We will rerun after their content owner adds missing terminology, and label that as a content change.

threads.title: Private channel document no longer appears

messages.text: Morrow user left #leadership yesterday and says the quarterly plan vanished from search. They can still find company-wide docs. Is this the permission incident?
This is expected after the SEC-18 fix. A user who loses channel membership must lose access to its indexed content. Confirm with the channel owner before requesting any permission change.
Replied with that explanation. We should not restore access just to make a search result reappear; the source system owns membership.

threads.title: Demo data for the healthcare call

messages.text: Harbor Health expansion call at 19:00 UTC. Should I use the current customer workspace to show a realistic clinical-policy search?
Use the synthetic demo tenant. It has invented policies and staff, and the demo user only sees public sample channels. No customer documents or patient information should appear.
Thanks. I will focus on internal policy discovery and explicitly say Beacon is not a clinical decision tool.
Beacon 1.8 canary pushed search p95 from 680ms to 1.9s. The new citation formatter is doing one source lookup per result. Holding rollout at 5%.
Batching source IDs into one query brings p95 down to 720ms in the same replay. Embedding latency is flat, so changing the model will not address this.
Patch passed the load replay. Rollout can resume after support office hours; rollback switch remains search_formatter_v2=false.
Morrow's champion moved teams. Weekly active use fell from 63% to 28% over three weeks, but the remaining users still rate results well. Renewal is November 1.
This looks like a sponsorship gap, not simply a search-quality problem. Can we get a new owner and hold two role-specific enablement sessions?
I know their operations director from the original deal. I will make an introduction; let's avoid leading with another discount before we understand adoption.

threads.title: Webhook retries creating duplicate usage events

messages.text: Stripe resent the same event three times after a timeout. Our metering worker counted it three times because dedupe used request ID instead of event ID. Issue BILL-62.
Please preserve the original event ledger. I need to identify invoices affected before we issue credits, not silently rewrite the finance export.
Unique index on provider + event ID is in place. Replay skipped duplicates and retained the first event. Riley has the affected tenant list; invoice corrections are owned by Operations.

threads.title: Two charges for the same usage period

messages.text: Birch Retail sees an overage amount that is triple their own request count. Invoice INV-SIM-204 is still open. Could the usage dashboard be lagging?
Engineering found duplicate metering events in BILL-62. I am reconciling the affected ledger and will issue a corrected invoice. Do not ask Birch to pay the disputed amount.
Customer has the investigation reference and a next update by Monday 18:00 UTC. I will keep the ticket open until they acknowledge the correction.

threads.title: What counts toward the query allowance?

messages.text: LumenGrid asked if a search returning zero results still consumes a query. They are sizing a launch-day usage spike and need a straight answer.
A successfully processed search counts even when it finds nothing. Validation failures and failed requests are not billable. The usage window resets on the subscription billing date.
I will put those examples in the quote. Query allowance is pooled across the workspace; it is not a separate quota for each employee.

threads.title: Birch account health during billing correction

messages.text: Birch's admin is upset about the overage invoice. Product use is growing, so the health score alone masks the relationship risk. Marking the account yellow until reconciliation is complete.
I am checking BILL-62 against the event ledger. We will send the corrected amount and an explanation together, rather than several partial numbers.
I will own the customer call. Support owns the ticket, Finance owns the amount, and CSM owns making sure their stakeholder feels heard.
BILL-62 affected three open invoices after duplicate Stripe events inflated usage. I have paused automatic collection for those invoices while we reconcile the immutable event ledger.
The dedupe patch is deployed. Use provider event IDs for reconciliation; request IDs differ across retries. Original events are retained for the audit trail.
Riley owns corrected amounts and customer credits. Support should reference the incident number, while CSM coordinates calls for sensitive accounts.
Juniper's intranet calls our search API on every keystroke. Their burst hits the tenant rate limit and returns HTTP 429. They read that as a daily quota exhaustion.
Can we raise the limit for the launch? They have 80 employees testing at once.
First debounce input and honor Retry-After with jitter. The error is a short-term rate limit, not their subscription allowance. Repeated immediate retries make the burst worse.
Restored last night's snapshot into an isolated environment. Beacon search was usable after 47 minutes. The last eleven minutes of ingestion were absent, matching the snapshot window.
Connector cursors resumed without replaying the whole workspace. One secret reference still pointed to production; the restore job now requires an explicit target secret map.
Runbook updated. Measured recovery time: 47 minutes; observed data gap: 11 minutes. These are exercise results, not a new customer SLA.
Flint Works has 35 users and needs SAML. I marked them as Growth because of seat count, but I cannot find the SSO switch in that demo tenant.
SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are Enterprise features. Growth still supports Google and Microsoft sign-in; those are not the same as customer-managed SAML.
I will demo the Enterprise tenant and explain the packaging before they invest time in a pilot. Do not promise a one-off feature flag as part of the Growth quote.
Workshop completed with twelve Harbor team leads. Everyone could find the revised leave policy. The most common question was how to tell whether a result is current.
Show the source timestamp and open the underlying document when policy timing matters. A search score tells us relevance, not that a policy is still approved.
No fresh ingestion complaints since September 15. I will leave the freshness monitor on through their onboarding week.
Birch INV-SIM-204 is corrected from $360 to $120 in overage charges. The duplicate $240 was voided before collection, so this is an invoice correction rather than a refund.
Updated the ticket with the revised invoice and the event-deduplication explanation. Waiting for their admin to confirm receipt.
Admin acknowledged the correction on our call. I will keep the account yellow through the next billing check, then reassess the relationship risk.

EU tenant documents and search indexes stay in eu-west-1. The current telemetry pipeline still sends aggregate request counts and latency to our US operations account. It does not include document text.
Summit Legal asked for every service, including operational logs, to stay in the EU. Can I mark their residency requirement as supported?
No. Full EU-only telemetry is on the roadmap, with no committed date. Please separate regional content storage from their stricter all-services residency requirement in the proposal.

threads.title: Residency requirement changes the Summit forecast

messages.text: Summit Legal clarified that all telemetry must remain in the EU, not just indexed content. Engineering confirmed our current deployment does not meet that requirement.
Moving this deal out of the September committed forecast. I will ask whether their reviewer accepts the current boundary, but there is no technical delivery date we can offer.
Correct. Please keep “full EU-only service” out of the order form until the telemetry work is scoped and approved.
Flint reduced the median equipment-procedure lookup from six minutes to two in a supervised ten-person exercise. Their sponsor wants to quote that as a company-wide productivity gain.
Please include the sample size and supervised setting. We have not measured all employees or a full month of regular use.
Agreed. The review should celebrate the exercise result and propose a broader measurement, without turning it into an unsupported ROI claim.
Our new support hire starts October 5. Laptop shipment is confirmed. Please approve the standard Support access group; production database access is not in that bundle.
Engineering can provide read-only diagnostic dashboards. Any production access needs a named owner, expiration date, and a separate approval tied to a specific task.
Use the onboarding checklist so access is attributable and easy to revoke later. No shared admin accounts for convenience.

threads.title: Scanned PDFs are missing from results

messages.text: Our PDF extractor reads text layers; it does not run OCR. A scanned invoice can upload successfully and still contain zero indexable words. We should expose that state.
Birch Retail hit exactly this. The upload says complete, which they interpret as searchable. A specific warning would save a support round trip.
Added “No text detected” to ingestion diagnostics. Workaround is to OCR the scan before upload. Native OCR remains a planned feature, not part of release 1.8.

threads.title: Scanned invoices uploaded but cannot be found

messages.text: Birch's September invoices upload successfully, but searching the vendor names returns nothing. All sample PDFs are image scans, and copied text comes back blank.
The extractor currently needs a text layer. Ingestion diagnostics now shows “No text detected.” Please ask them to run OCR and reupload one sample before processing the rest.
One OCR-processed file is now searchable by vendor name. Shared that workaround and explained that automatic OCR is not yet available.
Search infrastructure spend is 14% above September plan. Most of the increase is staging capacity left running overnight, not customer query volume.
I found two staging replicas from the load test. We can schedule them down outside working hours and retain one for incident reproduction.
Approved. Track savings after a full week; avoid presenting a projected reduction as already realized. Production redundancy stays as designed.
LumenGrid forwarded yesterday's export link to another admin. It now returns expired link. The customer worries the export itself was erased.
Download URLs expire after 24 hours. An authorized admin can generate a new link from the export job. Also, a forwarded link does not grant a different user access.
Confirmed a new link works for the requesting admin. Explained the difference between URL expiry and source-document retention.
Alder chose to stay with their built-in wiki search. They liked the cross-source demo, but only have one content system and could not justify another vendor.
Logging the loss reason as insufficient cross-source need, not missing integration. I will stop the generic follow-up sequence.
Good signal for qualification: ask how many systems staff search and how often permissions complicate discovery before scheduling a technical demo.
New Morrow champion confirmed: fictional operations manager Taylor Ames. First enablement session is September 29, focused on dispatch procedures rather than a tour of every feature.
For the renewal plan, track weekly active use, two concrete successful workflows, and whether the new champion can troubleshoot source access. Keep a weekly check-in through October.
I will bring three dispatch questions and ask users to try them themselves. If they cannot find the source, we will capture a reproducible example.
For a customer-visible outage, the on-call engineer owns technical recovery, Support owns the status updates, and CSM handles account-specific follow-up. One incident lead coordinates the timeline.
I will post updates every thirty minutes during active impact, even if the update is that we are still investigating. We should distinguish confirmed facts from hypotheses.
Account teams will link to that update rather than invent separate recovery estimates. The post-incident note should include impact, resolution, and prevention work.
Juniper Travel needs to rotate its automation key. The tenant can hold two active keys at once, so there is no reason to swap secrets during a maintenance window.
Create the replacement, deploy it to the caller, confirm traffic using the new key ID, then revoke the old one. Never paste either key into a Slack thread.
Added that order to the runbook. Revoking a key is immediate for new requests; existing in-flight requests may finish.
Alder's pilot is ending and their admin requested deletion. They want written confirmation after the workspace and connectors are removed, not just their subscription canceled.
Open the verified deletion workflow. Disable connectors, revoke tokens, delete active tenant data, and record the completion date. Backup expiry follows the documented 30-day retention cycle.
I will confirm the authorized requester and explain the backup window before Operations starts. Cancellation and data deletion are separate actions.

threads.title: Collecting a useful search bug report

messages.text: When escalating “search is wrong,” please include the query, expected source URL, user role, approximate time, and request ID. Customer document bodies should stay in the secure ticket attachment area.
Added a macro that asks whether the expected source opens for that same user. That catches permission problems before we call them ranking bugs.
Thanks. Remove access tokens from screenshots and headers. A request ID lets Engineering correlate logs without copying credentials into Slack.
LumenGrid signed Enterprise today: 180 seats, annual term, start October 1. Primary champion is fictional IT lead Jamie Wells. Success target is cutting internal policy lookup time in half.
Please attach the agreed success criteria and integration inventory to the handoff. Sales promised Slack and Drive; SharePoint was discussed as a future option only.
Kickoff booked for October 2. I will baseline current lookup time before training and keep the roadmap discussion separate from contracted deliverables.
LumenGrid kickoff is October 2. I need a Slack admin, a Drive admin, and the policy-content owner in the room. Without all three, we can connect systems but cannot validate useful results.
Use the agreed target: halve policy lookup time from their own baseline. We have no baseline measurement yet, so do not put a fabricated starting number on the success plan.
Handoff is complete: Slack and Drive in scope, 180 Enterprise seats. SharePoint was not sold as a launch integration.

Alder's verified deletion request is complete for active systems. Connectors were disabled, tokens revoked, and tenant records deleted today. Backup copies expire by October 28 under the 30-day policy.
I will send confirmation with both dates. The subscription cancellation was already processed; this closes the separate data-removal request.
Confirmed no connector jobs remain for the tenant. Restore procedures retain the deletion marker so an older backup cannot silently reactivate this workspace.

threads.title: Search evaluation before the October release

messages.text: We have 80 anonymized, permission-safe queries in the retrieval evaluation set. The candidate ranker improves top-five source recall from 71% to 79%, but acronym-only queries still regress.
Please break the result out by query type. One overall average could hide the failure mode that our support team sees most often.
Done: natural-language questions improved; short product-code lookups dropped four points. Holding the candidate until exact identifier matching has a separate path.
October rota is ready for review. Please confirm swaps by Friday so payroll has the correct on-call allowance. The engineer who accepts a swap must acknowledge it in the rota.
Maya is primary the first week, Theo is secondary. Swapping a calendar event alone does not update the paging schedule; I will reconcile both after approval.
Support has the contact list. If a page is not acknowledged in ten minutes, we follow the escalation chain rather than sending repeated direct messages.

threads.title: Prospect wants a search API example

messages.text: Juniper's architect wants to embed retrieval in their intranet. Show the search API response with source IDs, snippets, and relevance scores; they will build their own presentation layer.
Should I describe the relevance score as the probability that an answer is correct?
No. It is a ranking signal for similarity. A high score does not certify the source is current or correct. The integration should preserve citations and source permissions.
Cedar reran the same twenty questions after its content owner added an acronym glossary. Seventeen now return the right source in the first five; baseline was fourteen.
That clears the sixteen-question gate. We should credit the glossary work as well as the product instead of claiming a model change made the difference.
I will send the scorecard with the original queries and source links. Next decision is whether their sponsor approves a paid rollout, not another free pilot extension.
I am out from 18:00 to 20:00 UTC for a dentist appointment. Nina owns incoming tickets; Sam is the escalation backup. Current queue: six normal-priority requests, no active incident.
Got it. I will keep the Birch invoice follow-up with Riley so the customer does not receive two different financial explanations.
I will watch the incident channel. Please page only if there is a new outage or access leak; routine how-to questions can stay in the queue.
Friday lunch order closes at noon tomorrow. Vegetarian and gluten-free options are on the form. Please add your choice there so I do not miss replies scattered across threads.
I am remote Friday, so remove me from the headcount. Thanks for checking before ordering the usual amount.
Added mine. We have two visitors from the design workshop; I will enter their choices separately and mark the cost to team events.
